extension.description: Reviews container lifecycle, cleanup, execution, network, and persistent-data operations that can expose credentials or mutate host state.
extension.name: Container runtime protection

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of Docker builder or Buildx cache data.
permissions.label: Container build-cache prune
safer_guidance: Inspect builder disk usage and prune only cache that is safe to rebuild.

permissions.description: Identifies removal of Buildx builder instances and their local state.
permissions.label: Buildx builder removal
safer_guidance: Inspect active builders and switch away from the target builder before removal.

permissions.description: Identifies Compose cleanup that explicitly removes volumes or images in addition to services.
permissions.label: Compose persistent-data cleanup
safer_guidance: Run ordinary Compose teardown first and remove volumes or images only after reviewing retained data.

permissions.description: Identifies arbitrary command execution inside an existing running container.
permissions.label: Container command execution
safer_guidance: Use a read-only inspection command and avoid exposing host or credential material.

permissions.description: Identifies immediate signal delivery to running containers, including the default SIGKILL.
permissions.label: Container kill
safer_guidance: Use a graceful stop with an appropriate timeout unless an immediate signal is required.

permissions.description: Identifies bulk deletion of stopped containers.
permissions.label: Stopped-container prune
safer_guidance: List stopped containers and remove only reviewed container IDs.

permissions.description: Identifies removal of named containers after they have been stopped.
permissions.label: Container removal
safer_guidance: Inspect the named container and preserve any required logs or data before removal.

permissions.description: Identifies stopping running containers, which can interrupt active workloads.
permissions.label: Container stop
safer_guidance: Verify the exact container and its workload dependencies before stopping it.

permissions.description: Identifies reads of local container client authentication configuration.
permissions.label: Container credential access
safer_guidance: Pass only the specific credential material required by the operation.

permissions.description: Identifies container operations that can expose credentials or mutate protected state.
permissions.label: Sensitive container operation
safer_guidance: Use a pinned image, minimal privileges, and a preview where the command supports one.

permissions.description: Identifies forced removal that can terminate a running container without a graceful stop.
permissions.label: Forced container removal
safer_guidance: Stop the named container gracefully, inspect it, then remove that exact container.

permissions.description: Identifies bulk deletion of unused container images.
permissions.label: Container image prune
safer_guidance: List dangling or unused images and remove reviewed image IDs explicitly.

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of local container images by ID, tag, or alias command.
permissions.label: Container image removal
safer_guidance: List image references and remove only the exact reviewed image or tag.

permissions.description: Identifies bulk deletion of unused Docker networks.
permissions.label: Container network prune
safer_guidance: List unused networks and remove reviewed network names explicitly.

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of Docker networks that can disconnect dependent workloads.
permissions.label: Container network removal
safer_guidance: Inspect connected containers and remove only the exact unused network.

permissions.description: Identifies command execution with extended privileges inside an existing container or service.
permissions.label: Privileged container command execution
safer_guidance: Run without --privileged and grant only the narrowly required capability.

permissions.description: Identifies containers launched with broad host-level privileges.
permissions.label: Privileged container execution
safer_guidance: Grant only the required capabilities and keep host devices and filesystems isolated.

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of Swarm services, stacks, nodes, secrets, or configs.
permissions.label: Swarm resource removal
safer_guidance: Inspect the exact Swarm object and dependent workloads before removing it.

permissions.description: Identifies broad cleanup of unused containers, networks, images, build cache, and optional volumes.
permissions.label: Container system prune
safer_guidance: List the targeted container resources and prune one resource class at a time.

permissions.description: Identifies bulk deletion of unused local volumes.
permissions.label: Container volume prune
safer_guidance: List unused volumes and remove only reviewed names after confirming data retention.

permissions.description: Identifies deletion of named local volumes and their persisted data.
permissions.label: Container volume removal
safer_guidance: Inspect volume consumers and back up required persistent data before deletion.

extension.description: Reviews the showtime video-studio CLI's commands that reach beyond the video project: installing tools and models (setup), writing other coding agents' configuration (install), deleting files (setup --prune, clean, voice cache --clear), explicit network downloads (audio music|lib|packs fetch, assets media fetch, reference <URL>) and driving a headless browser against a site or a walkthrough script (site capture|component|record, demo record). Project-local commands (new, check, render, qa, export, look, snap, receipt, doctor, guide, status) and --help are not matched and remain automatic. Components that ordinary commands fetch on first use (for example a speech model on the first transcription) are outside this extension; `showtime setup --plan` lists them.
extension.name: showtime command protection

permissions.description: Identifies `showtime setup`, which downloads and installs ffmpeg, a Python virtual environment, Node packages, a headless browser and speech/vision models into ~/.showtime (a few hundred MB for the default core tier; about 3.6 GB with --full or --tier full; --with extras such as asr-turbo add up to 1.5 GB each; --fetch pulls named first-use components; --link writes ~/.claude/skills/showtime). --list, --plan and --estimate only print and exit before installing anything.
permissions.label: showtime tool and model install
safer_guidance: Run `showtime setup --estimate` or `showtime setup --plan` first: they print every download (URL, size, sha256) and install nothing.

permissions.description: Identifies `showtime install`, which adds a skill link, crew agent files and an MCP server entry to another coding agent's user-level or project configuration (for example ~/.codex, ~/.cursor, .gemini), or removes them with --uninstall. --print and --list change nothing.
permissions.label: showtime install into another coding agent
safer_guidance: Run the same command with --print first; it shows every file and config entry it would write and changes nothing.

permissions.description: Identifies showtime commands that delete files: `showtime setup --prune` (superseded files under ~/.showtime), `showtime clean` (a job's or project's intermediates; an agent can only delete with --yes because the confirmation needs a terminal) and `showtime voice cache --clear|--prune` (cached speech). Each removes only files showtime created; --dry-run and the print-only setup flags remove nothing.
permissions.label: showtime file removal
safer_guidance: Run `showtime clean --dry-run` (or `showtime setup --plan`) first to see exactly what would be removed and how much space it frees.

permissions.description: Identifies showtime commands whose purpose is to download from the network now: `audio music fetch` (produced music from creators' sites; --all is the whole catalog), `audio lib fetch` (the audio library, ~249 MB core tier), `audio packs fetch` (sound-effect packs; --all), `assets media fetch` (a CC0/public-domain image or video, or any http(s) URL given with --license) and `reference <http(s) URL>` (downloads a reference video to analyse).
permissions.label: showtime explicit network downloads
safer_guidance: Search first (`showtime audio music search`, `audio packs list`, `assets media search`) and fetch only the items the video uses.

permissions.description: Identifies `showtime site capture|component|record`, which drive a headless Chrome against a URL (loading the live site, dismissing cookie banners, downloading its images, logos and videos), and `showtime demo record`, which imports and runs a Node.js walkthrough script that clicks and types in a web app while it records frames.
permissions.label: showtime headless browser against a site or script
safer_guidance: Capture a local build with --serve <dir> where possible, and read the demo script before recording it.

rules.description: Identifies `showtime setup` (skills/showtime/setup/setup.py), which installs or updates tools and models in ~/.showtime and downloads what they need. --help, --list, --plan and --estimate return before the installer runs.
safer_alternatives: Run `showtime setup --estimate` or `showtime setup --plan` first.
rules.title: showtime setup install

rules.description: Identifies `showtime install` (skills/showtime/lib/st/cli_install.py), which writes or, with --uninstall, removes a skill link, crew agents and an MCP server entry in another coding agent's configuration. --print and --list change nothing.
safer_alternatives: Run the same command with --print first.
rules.title: showtime install into an agent

rules.description: Identifies `showtime setup --prune` (skills/showtime/setup/setup.py), which deletes files from older showtime versions that nothing uses any more under ~/.showtime.
safer_alternatives: Run `showtime setup --plan` or `showtime doctor` first to see what is installed.
rules.title: showtime setup --prune

rules.description: Identifies `showtime clean` (skills/showtime/lib/st/cli_job.py), which deletes the intermediates showtime wrote in a job or project (frame dumps, scratch, audio intermediates, with --all also review packs and logs). Without a terminal it refuses unless --yes is given; --dry-run only lists.
safer_alternatives: Run `showtime clean --dry-run` first.
rules.title: showtime clean

rules.description: Identifies `showtime voice cache --clear` and `--prune` (skills/showtime/lib/st/cli_voice.py), which delete cached narration lines; plain `showtime voice cache` only reports its size.
safer_alternatives: Run `showtime voice cache` first to see the cache size and cap.
rules.title: showtime voice cache clear or prune

rules.description: Identifies `showtime audio music fetch`, `audio lib fetch` and `audio packs fetch` (skills/showtime/lib/st/cli_audio.py), which download music tracks, audio-library tiers or sound-effect packs into ~/.showtime now. `audio lib fetch --list-parts` only lists.

safe_variants.title: showtime audio lib fetch part listing (--list-parts)

safer_alternatives: Search or list first and fetch only the items the video uses.
rules.title: showtime audio downloads

rules.description: Identifies `showtime assets media fetch` (skills/showtime/lib/st/cli_capture.py, skills/showtime/lib/st/assets/media.py), which downloads an image or video by search id, or any http(s) URL when --license is given, and writes a license sidecar and credit.
safer_alternatives: Use `showtime assets media search` first and fetch a result by its id.
rules.title: showtime assets media fetch

rules.description: Identifies `showtime reference <http(s) URL>` (skills/showtime/lib/st/cli_variety.py, skills/showtime/lib/st/variety/reference.py), which downloads a video from a direct link before analysing it. A local file path is not matched.
safer_alternatives: Download the reference yourself from a source you may keep, then pass the local file.
rules.title: showtime reference from a URL

rules.description: Identifies `showtime site capture|component|record` (skills/showtime/scripts/site.mjs), which load a URL in headless Chrome, dismiss consent banners and download the page's media. --serve <dir> captures a local static folder over 127.0.0.1 instead.
safer_alternatives: Capture a local build with --serve <dir> where possible.
rules.title: showtime site capture, component or record

rules.description: Identifies `showtime demo record` (skills/showtime/scripts/demo.mjs), which imports and runs a Node.js walkthrough script that drives a browser against --url or a --serve folder while recording frames.
safer_alternatives: Read the walkthrough script before recording it, and point it at a local build.
rules.title: showtime demo record

safer_alternatives: Use the print-only forms first: `showtime setup --estimate|--plan|--list`, `showtime install --print`, `showtime clean --dry-run`.
